fit.name: llama.cpp on the M1 Pro, fitted to this laptop

source: Engine bench tab of this page (llama.cpp, Homebrew build 11146, commit 7fe450e19, Metal), measured 2026-10-08 on the Apple M1 Pro
html:
Calibration on this laptop measured on Apple M1 Pro: Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M (391 MB) in llama.cpp with Metal and flash attention. One stream generates 198 tokens/s at an empty cache and 55.9 at 16,384 tokens of context (llama-bench, 3 repetitions): the slope gives 89% of the measured 165 GB/s. Decoding several sequences together (llama-batched-bench, 1 to 64 sequences) costs far more than the bytes say: keeping the single stream's 2.4 ms of fixed cost per step, a line through those steps adds 1.22 ms per sequence, where the vLLM fits on GPUs need no per-sequence term. Prompt processing at 512 tokens runs 3240 tokens/s, 81% of the 5.0 TFLOP/s measured peak. Then the planner simulates the bench tab's Poisson runs (llama-server, 16 slots, 413-token prompts, 128 output tokens; 30 requests each, so the p99 is the slowest one or two):

Requests/sRunsTPOT ms, measured / plannerTTFT p50 msTTFT p99 ms
0.527 to 8 / 8162 to 166 / 129227 to 285 / 262
1.029 to 15 / 11161 to 166 / 134255 to 326 / 359
1.5216 to 29 / 16162 to 187 / 139303 to 311 / 411
2.0229 to 47 / 24184 to 203 / 150318 to 675 / 2066
3.0244 to 49 / unstable271 to 410 / unstable1465 to 2727 / unstable
4.0250 to 51 / unstable319 to 389 / unstable2699 to 3667 / unstable
6.0150 / unstable591 / unstable4575 / unstable

Measured ranges span the repeated runs (the laptop was shared with other work; load averages 5 to 21). The planner follows the measurements up to about 1.5 requests per second and then saturates sooner and harder than the 30-request runs show: a short run never reaches the backlog a steady stream builds once the 16 slots are full, which the planner reports as unstable. The straight per-sequence line fits llama.cpp's batched steps from 1 to 16 sequences within about 15% but overestimates 32 and 64, beyond this server's 16 slots.

preset.name: Qwen3 0.6B on this M1 Pro, llama.cpp
preset.note: The laptop this page was built on: Qwen3-0.6B in llama.cpp's Q4_K_M with 16 server slots, constants fitted to the Engine bench tab's measurements (see the last section). Notice that memory is no constraint here (a 391 MB model beside 11.9 GB of cache room): llama.cpp's cost per decoding sequence and the TPOT target limit the traffic.

check: planner against the bench tab's Poisson runs at 0.5 to 4 requests/s: see the table in the M1 section below (measured on Apple M1 Pro).
